page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX-512F instructions, alongside AES cryptography. System memory consists of 23.0 GB of RAM, providing 5.75 GB per core. This instance includes a fractional GPU allocation of 0.25x NVIDIA T4 with 4 GB of dedicated VRAM, but does not include any local storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, the server ranks in the bottom 25%, reflecting its older Intel Xeon 8163 architecture. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with uncached read speeds of 19.82 GB/sec falling into the bottom 10%. Single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks, such as gzip and bzip3, also register in the bottom 10%. The fractional NVIDIA T4 GPU provides entry-level acceleration, achieving 233.71 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 64.28 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M parameter LLM, though larger models are not supported by this hardware profile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge offers an entry-level entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated accelerator. This resource density makes it suitable for lightweight graphical workloads, basic model inference, or development environments that require GPU APIs without the expense of a full GPU. However, the lack of local storage and the weak CPU and memory performance profiles present clear tradeoffs, making this instance unsuitable for high-throughput database operations, heavy data compilation, or large-scale parallel processing. Appropriate workloads include lightweight virtual desktops, entry-level AI inference prototyping, and basic web serving.
